title: Stereochemical Redundancy Inflates Benchmark Performance of Two-Dimensional Molecular Representations in Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction
abstract: Background: Machine learning models for blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability are routinely benchmarked on the B3DB dataset, with reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) frequently exceeding 0.90. Scaffold-based data splitting is widely regarded as sufficient protection against optimistic bias. We hypothesised that this protection is incomplete, because the two-dimensional (2D) molecular representations in general use cannot distinguish stereoisomers, which therefore remain effectively duplicated across scaffold-disjoint partitions.

title: Closed-loop artificial intelligence agents for animal epidemic prediction and decision support in livestock farming: a review
abstract: Animal diseases continuously threaten livestock production and public health, yet current surveillance approaches remain largely passive and fragmented. Conventional artificial intelligence models typically function as open-loop predictors, delivering static outputs that fail to accommodate the dynamic operational needs of veterinarians in real-world farm settings.

title: A Structure-Based Machine Learning Framework for Polymer Solar Cells: Prediction, Interpretation, and Virtual Screening
abstract: Polymer solar cells (PSCs) have attracted extensive attention due to their lightweight, flexibility, and solution-processability. However, the performance of PSCs arises from the intricate coupling of molecular structure, energy-level alignment, charge generation, transport, recombination, and morphology, posing a significant challenge for rational materials design. With the accumulation of experimental data and advances in polymer informatics, machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for accelerating PSC research.

title: ElectrolyteMD-Bench: How Well Do AI Agents Conduct Molecular Dynamics Studies across Electrolyte Solvation Regimes?
abstract: AI agents are advancing the automation of molecular dynamics (MD) research, with the potential to accelerate discovery and design of lithium-battery electrolytes. However, whether they can autonomously complete scientifically reliable electrolyte MD studies remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce ElectrolyteMD-Bench, which unifies dilute, high-concentration, and localized high-concentration electrolytes in a comparative study across distinct solvation regimes. The benchmark connects local coordination, ionic association, single-particle dynamics, and collective transport within one continuous research process. Agents autonomously perform system construction, equilibration, production sampling, property analysis, and interpretation under a frozen scientific model, while deciding whether to correct errors, continue sampling, or stop. We audit each study along four dimensions: simulation validity, analysis validity, evidence integrity, and outcome calibration. Across eight model--harness configurations, all 24 system runs produced valid production trajectories, yet none of the eight studies satisfied all scientific requirements. Failures included missing analyses, incorrect physical definitions or numerical implementations, insufficient statistical support, and completion claims inconsistent with retained evidence. These results expose a gap between successful MD workflow execution and reliable scientific study completion. ElectrolyteMD-Bench therefore provides a foundational test and defines a key capability threshold that autonomous electrolyte simulation must cross to advance toward computation-first materials exploration.

title: Pressure and temperature dependence of methane pyrolysis and hydrogen production in a micro flow reactor
abstract: Methane pyrolysis experiments were performed in a micro flow reactor to investigate the chemical mechanism sensitivities at elevated pressures and temperatures. The micro flow reactor used in this study provides independent control over reaction parameters. Experiments were performed at temperatures from 1400 to 1800 K and pressures from 1 to 10 bar at a fixed residence time of 60 ms. The yields of hydrogen, unreacted methane, and solid carbon were quantified for comparison to predictive models. The mass of heterogeneous depositions was also quantified. The presence of C2 and PAH species were measured by GC-MS. The results were compared to 1D simulations using a discrete sectional model for capturing the kinetics of particulate formation and surface deposition. The simulations replicated the pressure trend well at high temperatures (1800 K), but the sensitivity to temperature was in disagreement. Simulations generally found lower carbon and hydrogen yields and a stronger sensitivity to temperature than the experiment. An abundance of PAH intermediates was measured at lower temperatures and higher pressures. The simulated surface deposition rates were lower than the measured values but showed similar profiles. The results demonstrate the utility of micro flow reactors in recreating pyrolysis environments for hydrogen production from methane. The predictive capabilities of simulations could be improved by advancing the fuel decomposition and PAH formation and consumption kinetics at low temperatures and by detailed treatment of surface site density.

title: A Robust "Shrink-and-wrap" Piecewise Construction Transforms 3-Dimensional Mesh Structures into Mechanical Metamaterials
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials are materials that, by virtue of their microstructural architectures, exhibit mechanical properties not often found in nature: for example, auxetic mechanical metamaterials are materials that possess a negative Poisson's ratio in response to deforming forces. However, outside of relatively simple crystalline, lattice-based, or repeating-pattern architectures composed of mostly identical unit cells, mechanical metamaterials like auxetics are notoriously difficult to design, particularly across all three dimensions. Here we show that, for any structure that can be decomposed into triangular or tetrahedral meshes, those structures can be subjected to a simple transformation that that creates conditions within those triangular or tetrahedral simplexes that, regardless of their individual geometries, introduces a counter-rotating polygon/polyhedron mechanism that both guarantees a negative Poisson ratio and allows locally programmable mechanical properties. We apply this "shrink-and-wrap" construction to generate mechanical metamaterials from increasingly complex 3D structures, first from simple (convex) polyhedrons; then, to designs with arbitrarily large numbers of vertices and designed using constructive solid geometry (CSG) and 3D scanning; and, ultimately to 3D objects generated from videos captured by mobile phone camera -- making potentially any object or geometric structure designed or found in the real world transformable into a mechanical metamaterial. We show that these monolithic auxetic constructions remain readily 3D-printable via additive manufacturing techniques. We expect this piecewise approach to designing arbitrarily complex mechanical metamaterial structures can enable numerous potential applications where programmable internal reconfigurations and/or force redirection are required across and throughout their 3D geometries.

title: Decoding CO2 Adsorption Modes and CO Yield Variation on TM–N4 Single-Atom Catalysts via Constant-Potential Computation and Machine-Learning Investigation
abstract: Transition metal-based TM–N4 single-atom catalysts (SACs) are promising materials for electrochemical CO2 reduction reactions (CO2RR) toward CO formation. In this study, we employed the constant-potential method to investigate CO2 adsorption and reduction on 10 TM–N4 SACs (TM = Sc–Zn), with a particular focus on Ni–N4. We first evaluated the CO2 adsorption mode on the TM active site as a function of the applied electrode potential, U. Landau free energy analysis revealed a transition in CO2 adsorption mode from physisorption (D∞h–D2h) to chemisorption (C2v–C2v) at a critical electrode potential, referred to as the “transorption” potential (Utrans). Walsh diagram and machine-learning analyses revealed significant π*-orbital splitting and an unusual σ back-donation governing Utrans. We then examined the CO2RR processes by considering both adsorption modes of CO2. The transition from CO2 physisorption to chemisorption modes leads to a shift in the rate-limiting step from CO2 hydrogenation to CO desorption, the emergence of new active sites for competing hydrogen evolution reactions, and a decrease in electron transfer rates at more negative potentials. Taken together, these observations align with the experimental CO yield profile under increasingly negative potentials, capturing key performance trends of rise, plateau, and decline. Notably, the calculated Utrans values are consistent with the applied potentials at which CO yield declines for five SACs for which experimental data are available (Mn, Fe, Ni, Cu, and Zn). Thus, this work establishes Utrans as a novel predictive parameter for CO yield performance and offers valuable guidance for the design of advanced SACs in future studies.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Accelerating Lead Optimization away from Anti-Targets: Navigating the Structural Complexity of Promiscuous ADMET Proteins
abstract: The development of a small molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites, leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets.

title: Resolving Active Sites in Cu/ZnO Methanol Synthesis via Coupled Modelling of Surface Reconstruction and Coverage-dependent Kinetics
abstract: Identifying active sites in heterogeneous catalysis is central to fundamental understanding and designing catalysts, yet it becomes challenging when surface structures, adsorbate coverages and reaction kinetics co-evolve under operating conditions. This challenge is exemplified by the enduring controversy over the active site for methanol synthesis over ZnO/Cu catalysts. Here we combine global structure exploration, grand-canonical sampling, a reactive CuZnCHO machine-learning potential and coverage-consistent microkinetics to establish a condition-dependent picture of the active surface.

title: Interlayer Mismatch and Solvated Intermediates Control Spacer Mixing in 2D Perovskites
abstract: Organic spacer mixing is a versatile strategy for tuning the structure and properties of two-dimensional layered halide perovskites (2DLHPs), yet the factors that govern the resulting mixing configuration remain poorly understood. Here we investigate mixtures of alkyl monoammonium Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) and alkyl diammonium Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2DLHPs and identify three structural outcomes: alloying, phase separation, and superlattice formation.

title: Multimodal 3D imaging reveals a central role for lysosomes indissolution of cholesterol crystals by macrophages
abstract: Formation of cholesterol crystals (CCs) is a key event during the development of atherosclerosis, but the molecular mechanisms of their degradation within cells are poorly understood. By incorporating the fluorescent cholesterol analogue TopFluor-Cholesterol (TF-Chol) into CCs, we were able to visualize the uptake of CCs in macrophages using correlative fluorescence and soft X-ray microscopy. Using quantitative 3D live-cell imaging, we show that CCs are processed in late endosomes and lysosomes (LE/Lys), resulting in formation of TF-Chol containing lipid droplets (LDs) over time. Inhibition of lysosomal sterol export with U18666A caused accumulation of TF-Chol in LE/Lys, and inhibition of lysosomal acidification with bafilomycin A1 led to reduced dissolution of the CCs. Using a novel assay combined with 3D image processing, we show that large CCs in contact with macrophages are processed via lysosomal exocytosis followed by extracellular and intracellular degradation of CCs. Treating macrophages with a fluorescent version of cyclodextrin (CD) promoted the dissolution of CCs and enhanced the formation of LDs enriched with TF-Chol. The majority of fluorescent CD co-localized with a marker for LE/Lys during this process, suggesting that intracellular delivery to LE/Lys may contribute to the dissolution of CCs. Dehydroergosterol (DHE) is an intrinsically fluorescent sterol closely mimicking the properties and behavior of cholesterol. DHE is known to self-associate into aggregates and crystals, and by using fluorescence spectroscopy and specialized ultraviolet (UV) microscopy, we found that CD enhances the dissolution of DHE crystals in vitro and in cells. Together, our findings highlight the lysosomal pathway as responsible for dissolution of CCs, cholesterol trafficking, and efflux in macrophages.

title: Radical Disconnection Logic Enables Direct Conversion of α-Amino Acids into Differentiated Vicinal Diamines
abstract: Functional group interconversions (FGIs) are foundational to synthesis, yet classical acid-to-aminomethyl transformations remain intrinsically step- and redox-intensive. Here we introduce a radical disconnection strategy that enables the direct conversion of α-amino acids into differentiated vicinal diamines in a single step. The method relies on photocatalytic decarboxylation of readily available amino acids to generate α-amino radicals, which are selectively trapped by an in situ-formed, unstabilized N-protected formimine, a transient and previously inaccessible aminomethyl equivalent. This operationally simple approach circumvents harsh hydride reductions, tolerates hydride-sensitive functionalities, and offers broad generality. The robustness of the reaction is showcased by safe and intensified continuous-flow scale-up, with a >400-fold increase in space-time yield. Moreover, the differentiated diamines allow selective downstream functionalization and provide streamlined access to fragments of pharmaceutically active molecules. This work establishes radical disconnection as a powerful blueprint for redox-economical FGIs and unlocks a direct route to privileged vicinal diamine architectures.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Downstream evaluation of synthetic AI-generated T1-weighted contrast-enhanced MR images in glioma segmentation and grading
abstract: ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to evaluate synthetic T1 weighted post-contrast MR images generated from non-contrast-enhanced MR images, using deep learning (DL) methods, for automated brain tumor segmentation and automated classification of glioma grade based on imaging characteristics.Materials and methodsThree DL models were developed for synthesizing T1-weighted post-contrast MRI (T1ce) images using a publicly available dataset: (1) a conditional neural field with shift modulation (CoNeS) model, (2) a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM), and (3) a hybrid CoNeS + DDPM model. Five experimental settings were evaluated, incorporating combinations of real or synthetic T1ce and pre-contrast images. Synthetic T1ce images were evaluated in terms of image quality metrics, accuracy of tumor segmentation, and classification of cases into high-grade vs. low-grade glioma. Two classifier families were evaluated: (a) radiomics-based machine learning classifiers using random forest on extracted radiomic features, and (b) deep learning classifiers employing a convolutional neural network.ResultsThe combined CoNeS + DDPM model performed best in image quality and similarity metrics on the test set. Bootstrap analysis revealed that radiomics-based ML and deep learning-based classifiers exhibited distinct characteristics, each of which outperforming the other in different metrics.ConclusionsThe present study demonstrates significant advances in medical image AI synthesis by integrating stable diffusion and conditional neural fields, improving the overall quality of synthetic T1ce images. Nonetheless, synthetic images generated solely from pre-contrast sequences failed to consistently reproduce clinically relevant glioma features. As a result, current AI-generated T1ce images still lack the diagnostic fidelity required to replace true contrast-enhanced imaging in clinical practice.

title: Pressure-Induced Interlayer Bonding in Arsenic Revealed by Single-Crystal Synchrotron X-ray Diffraction in a Diamond Anvil Cell
abstract: Arsenic was studied by single-crystal synchrotron X-ray diffraction during room T compression up to 37.8 GPa across the rhombohedral (As–I, A7) to simple cubic (As–II, sc) phase transition, using a diamond anvil cell for pressure generation and He as a pressure-transmitting medium. The pressure dependence of the rhombohedral lattice parameter a, angle α, atomic position parameter u, and first (d1) and second (d2) neighbor distances provides experimental evidence for a two-step pressure-induced interlayer bond formation mechanism, underlying the transition from the layered A7 structure to the nonlayered simple cubic one. Consistent with phosphorus, our data demonstrate the existence of an intermediate pseudo simple-cubic (p-sc) structure between 26.5 and 31.8 GPa. Within this pressure interval, where α = 60° and u < 0.250, the progressive reduction of the interlayer distances (d1) and the corresponding elongation of the intralayer ones (d2) reveal a pressure-induced trans-influence effect, underpinning the transition from trigonal pyramidal to octahedral atomic coordination and relating the formation of the p-sc structure to the persistence of s-p orbital mixing and stereochemically active lone pair electron density. While solving a long-standing structural issue in As, this study provides in-depth chemical insights concerning bond theory in pnictogens and the synthesis of innovative As-based materials.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Azahelicenes via Rh-Catalyzed C–H Functionalization of 6-Hydroxyisoquinoline Derivatives with Alkynes
abstract: Herein, we report an asymmetric C–H functionalization of 6-hydroxyisoquinoline derivatives and annulation with internal alkynes. The reaction is catalyzed by a chiral cyclopentadienyl (Cp)-Rh complex in combination with a modified chiral amino acid. A series of azahelicenes is afforded in good yields (up to 93%) with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). A plausible catalytic cycle is proposed based on control experiments and DFT calculations, involving the reductive elimination from a high-valent Rh intermediate.

title: Fractal Colonization of Prebiotic Niches: Mechanical Budding of Nano-vesicles and Kinetic Resource Depletion as an Oncological Atavism
abstract: Periodic mechanical forcing of the early Earth, from lunar tides (period of about 10 h) and radiogenic geysers (about 15 min) to von Kármán vortex shedding (about 1 s), may have loaded fatty-acid protocell membranes on time scales comparable to their relaxation times. We present a minimal model in which the tension of a parent vesicle, relaxing with time constant τ under rectified periodic forcing, releases one nano-vesicle at each upward crossing of a budding threshold.

title: The Chemistry of the Golgi-Cox Stain
abstract: Our review provides both a theoretical discussion and experimental investigation of the Golgi–Cox stain. While this procedure has been a mainstay in the histologist’s toolkit for centuries and is implemented quite straightforwardly, there is still significant uncertainty around the chemistry. As such, it remains unclear how the stain works and, therefore, how it can be improved to be safer, faster, more reliable and work for larger specimens. Here, we provide technical and chemical considerations supplemented with original experimental observation on tissue clearing methods.

title: A Molecular View of Framework-Associated Zeolite Lewis Acid Sites: Linking Structure to Meerwein–Ponndorf–Verley Reactivity
abstract: The Meerwein–Ponndorf–Verley (MPV) reaction has been used to probe the Lewis acidity and local environment of aluminum Lewis acid sites (LAS) in zeolites and how these properties evolve upon post-synthetic treatments such as calcination and steaming. However, directly linking catalytic activity to proposed framework-associated aluminum LAS remains challenging because the identity of the catalytically relevant species is often inferred indirectly from correlations between spectroscopic signatures and reactivity.

title: Dynamic Ni–Fe Interfaces Regulate Stimulated Geological Hydrogen Production
abstract: Geological hydrogen (Geo-H2) generated by water-rock redox reactions could expand low-carbon hydrogen resources by tapping reducing equivalents stored in subsurface minerals. Stimulated Geo-H2 production remains difficult to engineer because the reaction sequence connecting rockhosted Fe2+ release to H2 evolution is incompletely constrained. Here, we support an interfacial sequence linking olivine Fe2+ release, an Fe(II)-bearing hydroxide intermediate state, Fe3O4bearing product growth, and Ni redistribution at evolving Fe-rich interfaces.

title: Molecular Dynamics Studies of Model Ionizable Lipids in an mRNA Vaccine
abstract: Effective COVID-19 mRNA vaccines encapsulate nucleoside-modified messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA), which encodes the prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, inside lipid nanoparticles. Endosomal acidification motivates the study of ionizable lipid protonation. Here, we isolate how protonation changes hydration, solvent preference, and structural organization of ALC-0315 in simplified model environments. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we identify clear protonation-dependent differences in lipid orientation, hydration, and collective organization across three model systems.

title: Bidirectional Refractive-Index Programming via Three-Stage Sequential Thiol-Click Chemistry for High-Performance Holographic Recording
abstract: Conventional holographic photopolymers (HPs) mainly rely on a polymerization–diffusion mechanism to record volume holographic gratings (VHGs), resulting in trade-offs among photosensitivity, refractive-index (RI) modulation (Δn), optical clarity, and VHG stability. To address these trade-offs, we propose a bidirectional refractive-index programming (BRIP) strategy based on three sequential thiol-click reactions. Stage I employs a base-catalyzed thiol–acrylate Michael addition to form a thiol-rich host matrix.

title: μ-Oxo-Bridged Iodine(III) Reagents Enable Catalyst- and Light-Free Fluoro(halo)methyl Radical Generation
abstract: While conventional radical fluoroalkylation typically requires exogenous catalysts or photoactivation to overcome significant kinetic barriers, here we report bench-stable μ-oxo-bridged iodine(III) reagents that release fluoro(halo)methyl radicals upon heating without an external catalyst, additive, or light. The resulting radicals initiate cascade cyclizations of methacrylamides and methacrylohydrazides to afford fluorinated oxindoles, pyrazolones, and related heterocycles.

title: DNA-Encoded Chemical Diversification of mRNA Display Libraries
abstract: mRNA display can survey vast peptide populations, but the chemical diversity available to selection remains largely constrained by translation. DNA-encoded libraries possess the complementary advantage: synthetic diversity can be introduced through split-and-pool chemistry, although without the peptide scaffolds and evolutionary framework provided by translation. Here, we combine these approaches by performing DNA-encoded chemical diversification directly on mRNAdisplayed peptides.

title: Acoustic Optimization and Standardized Fabrication of a Biomimetic Liver Phantom for Quantitative Multimodal Imaging
abstract: We previously developed a structurally biomimetic liver phantom composed of alginate units that reproduce the scale and organization of hepatic lobules. Here, we optimized the non-steatotic baseline formulation and fabrication workflow to more closely reproduce normal liver properties across ultrasound, CT, and MRI. The updated formulation was evaluated using clinical imaging systems, followed by quantitative water-tank characterization of speed of sound (SoS) and attenuation coefficient (AC).

title: Optimizing Affinity and Pharmacokinetics of a Cysteine-sulfoxide Derivative as Potential Inhibitor of BACE-1 using Fragment Growing and Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Alliin (S-(2-propenyl)-L-cysteine sulfoxide) was initially identified as a potential inhibitor of BACE-1, with the ability to chelate the catalytic dyad, but with very poor pharmacokinetics. We aimed to optimize these pharmacokinetic parameters, with a possible gain in affinity by growing the ligand towards the sub-pocket of the active site under the flaps. We employed fragment growing, implemented in the ligand designer module of Schrodinger, to extend 2-propenyl-alliin (a derivative of alliin) from both ends, with the multiparameter optimization (MPO) score as a guide.

title: Selective and Modular Synthesis of N1 and C3 Dialkylated Indoles via Iridium-Catalyzed Hydrogen Borrowing
abstract: An iridium-catalyzed strategy for the modular synthesis of N1,C3-dialkylated indoles from readily available alcohols and indolines is presented. The method enables the selective installation of two distinct substituents via N-alkylation, dehydrogenation, and C-alkylation. Mechanistic studies support a borrowing hydrogen pathway that overcomes the challenging C-alkylation of N-protected indoles.

title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing the domain to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC.

title: Reconfigurable Flow Reactors Assembled from 3DPrinted Self-Healing Hydrogel Modules
abstract: Here, we introduce millimeter-scale fluidic reactors assembled from digital-light-processing (DLP)-printed self-healing hydrogel modules. A poly(acrylic acid-co-2-acrylamidophenylboronic acid)/poly(vinyl alcohol) formulation combines photoprintability with dynamic interfacial association. Printed modules contain straight, curved, branched, looping, and crossing channels, as well as mixing chambers. When brought into contact under ambient conditions, separate modules form liquid-tight interfaces that support continuous flow.

title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
abstract: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs.

title: Computer Vision for Predicting Electrochemical Reaction Performance from Electroanalytical Data
abstract: Electrosynthesis has surfaced as a key approach in modern synthesis, enabling more sustainable chemical transformations with reduced chemical waste. The accurate prediction of electrosynthesis performance is crucial for accelerating the discovery and design of reactions. Despite indisputable advances, the descriptor-based predictions fall short in representing the full reaction regime due to the high‑dimensional parameter space of electrosynthesis. Cyclic voltammograms, which are typically employed for mechanistic analysis, inherently contain rich information about electrochemical processes.

title: Pt(II)-Flavin Complexes As Anticancer And Antibacterial Agents
abstract: We report a new chelating pyridyl–imine ligand bearing a riboflavin-derived pendant group and its Pt(II) complexes 1 and 2, designed as cisplatin- and oxaliplatin-like derivatives. Both complexes reacted with DNA and a histone-derived peptide, with 1 showing markedly higher covalent reactivity. However, this trend was not reflected in biological activity. Complex 2 displayed micromolar antiproliferative effects and pronounced antibacterial activity, particularly against Bacillus subtilis, whereas 1 was inactive in the tested models.

title: Estimand Divergence Between Static Docking and Molecular Dynamics as a Triage Filter for Antimalarial Leads
GITT Evaluation with PyBaMM
abstract: The accuracy of the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) for determining solidstate lithium diffusion coefficients was systematically evaluated using synthetic data generated with Doyle–Fuller–Newman model in PyBaMM. GITT-derived diffusion coefficients were compared with the known values used to generate the data across a broad range of possible material properties. GITT systematically underestimated the diffusion coefficient, with absolute errors increasing at higher diffusivities.

title: Exploration of Structure–Activity Relationships and Gut Restriction in Anti-Cryptosporidium Triazolopyridazine Series
abstract: Cryptosporidiosis is a major cause of diarrheal disease worldwide, particularly in young children and immunocompromised individuals, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. Previously, the triazolopyridazine derivative SLU-10482 was identified as a potent anti-Cryptosporidium lead, but it suffers from modest affinity for the hERG ion channel. In the present study, structure–activity relationships (SAR) were investigated through systematic modification of the 3-position of the aryl ring and by designing gutrestricted analogues intended to reduce systemic exposure while maintaining…

title: BET Bromodomain Pan-D1-Biased Inhibitors with Improved Drug-Like Properties and hERG Profiles as Therapies for Inflammatory Liver Injury
abstract: BET bromodomain inhibitors are efficacious as anti-inflammatory compounds, but clinical translation is hampered by dose-limiting toxicities from non-selective inhibition. We herein report compounds 16 and 26, based on previously reported 4-methyl-1,2,3-triazole-based inhibitor, DW34. 16 has a BRD4 BD1 Ki of 10 nM, and up to 13–38-fold selectivity for BRD4 BD1 over other BD2 domains, and an improved hERG affinity of 4.24 µM over DW34. 26, A biscyclopropyl analog of 16 showed further enhancement of BD1 selectivity over BD2 (26–203-fold), but exhibited more potent hERG inhibition.

title: Cobalt(III)-Catalyzed Synthesis of Aminoisoquinolones and Amino-2-Pyridones via C–H Functionalization with Ynamides: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study
abstract: Carbon–hydrogen (C–H) functionalization methodologies typically rely on electron-poor π-systems, whereas the engagement of electron-rich counterparts remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report the first cobalt-catalyzed, site- and regioselective C–H functionalization of O-phenyl hydroxamic acids with electron-rich ynamides to afford aminoisoquinolones and 2-pyridones.

title: Language-model-derived training data for polymer glass transition prediction: a controlled benchmark
abstract: Experimental polymer property data are scarce and costly, whereas large language models (LLMs) have absorbed much of the chemical literature and can be queried for a fraction of a cent per polymer. We ask whether LLM-produced data can replace or supplement experimental data for predicting the glass transition temperature (Tg). With Claude Sonnet 5 as the teacher we built two synthetic datasets for USD 10.28: a generated set of 7,912 polymers whose structures and Tg values were both written by the LLM, and a labeled set of 9,925 hypothetical PI1M polymers whose Tg the LLM predicted.

title: Differentiable mass transfer modeling enables wet lab validated inverse analysis of liquid chromatography
abstract: Liquid chromatography (LC) is essential to organic synthesis and emerging selfdriving laboratories (SDLs), yet LC method development remains cost-intensive and dependent on expert intuition. Mechanistic chromatographic models offer a route to transferable and data-efficient method development, but their practical use is limited by the computational cost of inverse modeling and by the ill-posedness of parameter estimation from experimental chromatograms. Here we report a wet-lab-validated differentiable physics framework for LC inverse modeling.

title: Framework Connectivity Tunes the Nuclear Spin Bath and Extends Coherence in Cu(II) Metal–Organic Framework Qubit Lattices
abstract: Designing solid-state spin-qubit arrays that retain long coherence at high spin density remains a central challenge in quantum information materials. In molecular qubits, this challenge arises because the same local coordination environment and lattice architecture that define the spin array also control the dominant decoherence channels, most notably nuclear-spin spectral diffusion and coupling to low-frequency phonons.

title: Closing the Loop Between Synthetic and Living Cells
abstract: Synthetic cells are moving beyond compartmentalised microreactors to become integrated components of biological networks that physically and chemically merge with their hosts. Existing reviews classify this field by mode of emission, by chemistry, or by architecture, and so describe the construct rather than its effect. This review takes the receiver's side, treating the functional adaptation of the living host as the readout of bio-hybrid function: how living cells probe their synthetic partners mechanically and adapt to them metabolically.

title: Photophysics and Triplet Sensitization of the Molecular Lanthanide YbQ3
abstract: The energy transfer mechanism between organic ligands and lanthanide-based near-infrared emitters, such as ytterbium ions (Yb3+), is of great photophysical interest. In recent years, lanthanides have attracted attention for their capacity for both up-and down-conversion for a range of applications. While lanthanides generally have extremely small absorption cross-sections, their light-matter interaction can be complemented by an appropriate choice of chromophore ligand.

title: StateFlux: Physically Validated Quantum Metabolic State Networks Reveal Limited Incremental Value for Toxicity Prediction
abstract: Mechanistic molecular representations are increasingly proposed as a route to improve toxicity prediction by supplementing parent structure with protonation, metabolism, and quantum-chemical reactivity. Whether those physically richer representations provide predictive information that is genuinely orthogonal to molecular structure remains uncertain. Here, StateFlux represents each drug as a network of chemical and predicted metabolic states with node-level GFN2-xTB properties and edge-resolved changes in ionization potential, electron affinity, electrophilicity, solvation, and local…

title: A Catalyst Discovery Workflow Coupling MLIP with MOBO for Nitrite-to-Hydroxylamine Electroreduction
abstract: The selectivity of electrocatalytic nitrite reduction to hydroxylamine is governed by multiple coupled steps within the multi-electron nitrogen–oxygen reduction network, which cannot be represented simultaneously by a volcano relation based on a single adsorption descriptor. To address this limitation, a catalyst discovery workflow coupling machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is developed.

title: Docking, Molecular Dynamics, QSAR, and Machine Learning in Alzheimer's Small-Molecule Drug Discovery: Current Utility, Key Limitations, and Reproducibility Challenges
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains one of the most challenging therapeutic areas for small-molecule drug discovery because of its multifactorial pathology, complex target biology, and demanding central nervous system drug-development requirements. In this context, computational methods have become increasingly important for compound prioritization, hypothesis generation, and structure–activity interpretation.

title: Predicting the Thermodynamic Stability of Ce/Ti Nanoclusters under Synthetic Conditions
abstract: Predicting which molecular species will form under a given set of synthetic conditions requires determining their thermodynamic stability relative to precursors and competing products. For complex molecular systems in solution, this requires both accurate electronic-structure calculations and sufficient configurational sampling. Here, we investigate two hexanuclear Ce/Ti clusters that form under different synthetic conditions: a yellow Ce IV 4 Ti 2 cluster obtained under mild conditions and a red Ce III 2 Ti 4 cluster, presented here for the first time, that requires higher temperature…

title: CuBr-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Decahydroquinoxaline-Based
abstract: A CuBr-catalyzed one-pot protocol provides access to decahydroquinoxaline-based bis(propargylamines) from readily available terminal alkynes, aromatic aldehydes, and a C2symmetric chiral diamine. The three-component coupling proceeds at 120 °C within 12 h, affording the products in 58–93% yields with diastereomeric ratios of up to 99:1. The synthetic utility of the protocol is illustrated by the ZnI2-mediated conversion of a representative bis(propargylamine) (7a) into the corresponding axially chiral allene (8a) with 90% ee.

title: Computationally Accelerated Discovery of Efficient Dual Component White Light Emitters
abstract: This work presents a computationally guided approach to formulating white light emission from a series of Hbonded iridium phosphors and a complementary H-bonding fluorophore. We computationally investigated thirty new Ir(III) complexes that all incorporate a previously studied H-bond rich biguanide functionalised ligand. The results of the computational screening, based on TD-DFT peak emission data and established lifetime and quantum efficiency data in the literature, identified seven Ir(III) candidates suitable for synthesis and further investigation.

title: Determining Which Phonons Affect Dynamic Disorder and Charge Mobility in Molecular Crystals
abstract: Organic semiconductors (OSCs), and especially molecular crystals, exhibit unique structural complexity and strong coupling between electronic and vibrational degrees of freedom. The strong electron-phonon coupling (EPC) localizes the charge carriers and limits the charge transport rate as a consequence of the dynamic disorder (σij). In principal, it should be possible to engineer new molecular crystals with reduced dynamic disorder, but determining which phonons contribute the most to dynamic disorder and what are the corresponding effects on charge transport has been elusive.

title: Highly Luminescent Alkyl- and Alkoxy-Terminated Silicon Quantum Dots via Aging Following Single-Step Plasma Synthesis and Functionalization
abstract: Nonthermal plasma synthesis enables the continuous production and immediate surface functionalization of silicon quantum dots (Si QDs) in a single, flow-through reactor. While this process occurs on a millisecond timescale, the resulting nanocrystals are often limited by low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) due to persistent surface defects. In this work, we demonstrate that a minimal post-treatment, aging the Si QDs in specific solvents, can enhance the PLQY to ~50%, approaching the performance of much more complex solution-phase methods.

title: A Pan-YTHDF Probe Enables Chemical Modulation and Dissection of RNA m6A Reader Programs
abstract: Genetic perturbation has been central to defining the functions of RNA modification binding proteins (readers), but knockout approaches remove the entire protein and cannot readily distinguish modification-dependent reader activity from other protein-associated functions. Small molecules provide an orthogonal strategy by directly perturbing the reader protein–RNA recognition event while preserving the reader protein. Here we report DF142, a cell-active pan-YTHDF chemical probe developed through an m6A-anchored design strategy.

title: Photo-oxidation of Dilute Methane in Dairy Barn Air: Pilot Scale Optimization
abstract: Low concentration (below 1000 ppm) methane emissions from point sources such as cattle barns remain a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions, and have proven hard to mitigate. Previously, a novel method for methane photo-oxidation using UV light to produce chlorine radicals from chlorine gas, which subsequently oxidize methane, was proposed. Here we present the first real-world experimental results from a pilot scale Methane Eradication Photochemical System (MEPS) deployed at a dairy farm in Denmark.

title: Chiral Patterning Drives Peptide Coacervate Formation in Coarse-Grained SIRAH Simulations
abstract: Peptide-based polyelectrolyte complexes (PECs) are a promising class of stimuli-responsive materials with applications in drug delivery. Yet, the molecular mechanism by which stereochemical patterning governs their phase behavior remains unresolved. Racemic chiral patterning is known to favor liquid coacervate formation over solid precipitation by disrupting the ordered β-sheet structure, but experimentally elucidating the molecular-level origin of the solution-phase selection remains challenging.

title: Origin of Reagent-Dependent Diastereoselectivity in Grignard Additions to a TADDOL-Derived α-Ketiminophosphonate
abstract: Grignard additions to a TADDOL-derived -ketiminophosphonate display pronounced reagent-dependent diastereoselectivity, with dr values of 94:6 for methylmagnesium bromide and 55:45 for 2-naphthylmagnesium bromide. In this study, we carried out DFT calculations showing that dimeric Grignard models coordinate to the phosphoryl and sulfonyl regions of the substrate, restricting C–P bond rotation and enabling facial differentiation.

title: Intramolecular N-Alkylation of O-Aryloximes Facilitates N–O Homolysis and Iminyl Radical Cyclization
abstract: An attempt to improve a microwave-promoted iminyl radical cyclization cascade targeting the Securinega alkaloid virosinine A revealed that the process could be initiated at lower temperatures (66 °C versus 100 °C) under Finkelstein conditions. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations indicate that Finkelstein bromination or iodination facilitates intramolecular N-alkylation. This lowers the N–O BDE of the substrate and permits homolysis at lower temperatures than previously observed.

title: A Convenient Crystalline Acyl Silane for the Colorimetric Titration of Diisobutylaluminum Hydride (DIBAL)
abstract: Due to the intense color associated with acyl silanes and their fast reaction with DIBAL to generate colorless alcohols, these properties were utilized to develop a colorimetric titration of DIBAL. A convenient crystalline acyl silane was identified that can be prepared on gram scale without the need for chromatographic purification by direct crystallization of the reaction products. Use of this material for the colorimetric titration of DIBAL and n-BuLi was possible. A variety of other 2 hydride and organometallic reagents were also tested and showed unsatisfactory endpoints.

title: One network to link them all: an untargeted multi-metabolomics-methods network
abstract: Metabolomics aims to cover a large range of metabolites from polar metabolites to hydrophobic lipids. Therefore, multiple chromatographic methods – such as reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) or hydrophilic interaction chromatography (HILIC) – are combined to provide a comprehensive overview. The resulting tables need to be combined afterward for data analysis, but several metabolites might be detected across multiple methods. Currently, it is only possible to deal with such multiple entries for identified metabolites.

title: Microchemical Strategies and AI-Enabled Biosensing for Non-Invasive Liquid Biopsy in Precision Oncology
abstract: Traditional blood-based liquid biopsy platforms have established crucial paradigms in precision oncology by enabling the longitudinal tracking of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and circulating tumor cells (CTCs). However, blood sampling remains minimally invasive, requires dedicated clinical infrastructure, and is restricted by physiological boundaries such as the blood-brain barrier (BBB).

title: Engineering Gold Nanoparticles for Transmembrane Anion Transport
abstract: Synthetic transmembrane ion transporters are traditionally classified as either ion channels or carriers. Here we introduce a new nanoparticle-based transporter architecture in which spherical gold nanoparticles densely decorated with flexible urea- and thiourea-based ion-binding arms efficiently mediate transmembrane anion transport, providing the first proof of principle for nanoparticle-based transmembrane anion transport.

title: eZacros: Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations for Electrochemical Catalysis
abstract: Free energy diagrams rank electrocatalysts thermodynamically but do not resolve which elementary step limits the rate under operating conditions, or how the surface coverage that governs that competition is established. Lattice kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) recovers both by treating elementary steps as stochastic events on an explicit lattice, but electrochemical kMC workflows remain far less standardized than the free-energy approaches common in computational electrocatalysis.

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Eight Ru-based catalytic hydrogenolysis configurations for the upcycling of waste polyolefins
abstract: In recent years, plastics demand has exceeded 400 million tons annually worldwide. Due to their mechanical and chemical resistance and low cost, polyolefins, including polyethylene (PE), represent beyond 50% of global plastic production, contributing to the generation and accumulation of plastic waste. Traditional waste management technologies, including landfilling and incineration, result into greenhouse gases emissions and potential loss of valuable carbon sources, whereas mechanical recycling strategies generally imply materials degradation and loss of mechanical properties.

title: Ferrier Rearrangement Intermediates Featuring Aliphatic Acyl Protecting Groups
abstract: The Ferrier rearrangement of 1,2-unsaturated monosaccharides (glycals) to 2,3-unsatured glycosides, is important for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and natural products. Mechanistically, the nucleophilic substitution proceeds via a cationic intermediate, the “Ferrier cation”, whose structure is difficult to capture with conventional analytical techniques. Here, we characterize the Ferrier cations of glucal and galactal building blocks involving aliphatic acyl protecting groups (pivaloyl-, levulinoyl- and chloroacetyl esters) using cryogenic gas-phase infrared spectroscopy.

title: Controlled Buildup of Multiply Charged Anionic Clusters at Interfaces Using Anion-Anion Reactions
abstract: Reactions between ions of identical polarity are usually prevented by a strong Coulomb barrier in the gas phase. Here, we systematically investigate the binding of gaseous reactive anions to anions at a vacuum layer interface and develop our findings into a method for the controlled build-up of highly charged molecular anions and nanoclusters. Following a previous observation of dimeric ions in trace amounts upon the mass-selective deposition of the reactive fragment anion [B 12 I 11 ] – , the procedure was optimized here to oligomerize such ions, resulting in highly charged anionic chains.

title: Increasing high-temperature creep life via improved directional solidification: A novel Ni-based single crystal superalloy reinforced by in-situ MC carbide fibers
Quantification of Levoglucosan in Biomass Burning Particulate Matter Using a Glucometer Test Strip
abstract: Levoglucosan (LG) is highly abundant in biomass pyrolysate and is widely used as a tracer for biomass burning in environmental sciences. Current analytical standards rely on gas or liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC/LC-MS). Because these methods are expensive, there is a critical need for low-cost alternatives. This work explores using commercial glucometer strips to detect and quantify LG by first converting it into d-glucose with heat and acid.

title: Steric Repulsion Driven Formation of a 3D Covalent Organic Framework Polymorph with Exceptionally High Surface Area
abstract: Dimensional polymorphism, in which the same molecular building blocks form frameworks of different dimensionality, offers a direct route to distinct pore architectures in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). True 2D/3D polymorphism remains rare, since linkers capable of forming both 2D and 3D COFs tend to favor 2D structures. Accessing 3D polymorphs remains a challenge. We investigated the dimensional polymorphism in an imine-linked COF based on a terphenyl tetraaldehyde linker core, which is functionalized with two bulky methyl benzoate groups, and p-phenylenediamine.

title: Localizing and quantifying the dynamic interfacial proton population in alkaline electrocatalysis
abstract: In alkaline electrocatalysis, electrostatic theory predicts, and experiments confirm, interfacial acidity that deviates from bulk pHb. The location and magnitude of the proton population within the electric double layer (EDL) and its evolution with catalytic turnover have remained unresolved, leaving a critical gap for mechanistic interpretation across proton-coupled electrocatalysis.

title: Integrating Pathway Engineering and FoTO1-Mediated Oxidation for Taxadien-5α-ol Production
abstract: Microbial reconstruction of paclitaxel biosynthesis is hindered by limited taxadiene (1) supply and poor selectivity in the first oxidative step. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli for the efficient de novo production of taxadien-5α-ol (2) by integrating enhanced taxadiene (1) biosynthesis with selective oxidation. Coordinated engineering of taxadiene synthase expression, precursor supply, pathway regulation, and geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase increased the titer of 1 7.5-fold, from 20.3 to 152.6 mg L−1.

title: Polymer Informatics in the Era of Foundation Models: From Representation to Autonomous Design
abstract: Foundation models, pretrained on broad datasets and adapted to multiple tasks, offer a way to reuse chemical knowledge across polymer property prediction and inverse design. Realizing this opportunity requires connecting learned representations to materials whose properties also depend on molecular populations, formulation, processing, and measurement conditions. Here, we review advances in polymer foundation models and the data, representations, and experimental workflows that support their use in materials design.

title: ProtMutMap: Predicting Protein Binding Free Energy Changes Using Multiple-Mutation Networks
abstract: Predicting changes in binding free energy ΔΔ G caused by multiple mutations at protein−protein interfaces requires accounting for nonadditive interactions between mutations, which an additive approximation based on single mutations cannot capture, and for the dependence on the computational pathway in stepwise approaches that introduce mutations sequentially. Here, we propose ProtMutMap, a method that integrates information from multiple pathways in a network whose nodes represent target variants and variants containing subsets of their mutations, and whose edges represent free energy…

title: Controlling polyethylene fibrillation in PFAS-free dry electrodes for processability and electrochemical performance
abstract: Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) is a more sustainable binder alternative to polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) for producing PFAS-free Li-ion battery electrodes using a solvent-free PE fibrillation process. We show that PE fibrillation is thermo-activated and can be controlled to produce an extensive network of nano-fibrils with a median size of 20-40 nm.

title: Residue-Conditioned In-Pocket Design for Paralogue Selectivity
abstract: Structure based generative model explore chemical spaces inside the protein active site , typically prioritizing candidates through empirical scoring functions.Few evaluate wthether the results is selective for the intended protein over a close paralogue , and none of them combines that evaluation with residue level conditioning and covalent bounds placement .

title: Integrative Physics and Machine Learning-Based Optimal Binding Pose Generator for Protein-Ligand Complexes
abstract: Accurately identifying the optimal protein–ligand binding pose is crucial for reliable binding affinity prediction, as molecular dynamics–based approaches are highly sensitive to the initial structure. However, there is currently no efficient way to predict such poses. Indeed, we assess the capabilities of three proposed AI-based software solutions (AlphaFold3, Boltz and RoseTTAFold All-Atom) and demonstrate their substantial shortcomings in this context.

title: Data-Efficient Machine Learning Potentials for Organic Reactions through Active-Learning-Guided Fine-Tuning
abstract: Transition states (TSs) are central to reaction barriers and mechanisms, yet their accurate localization remains computationally demanding. Reactive machine learning potentials can accelerate TS optimization by rapidly predicting potential energy surfaces, but achieving chemical transferability requires extensive sampling and quantum chemical (QC) labeling of reactive conformations.

title: A Dinucleating β-Thio-δ-Diiminate Ligand Enables Metal-Dependent CO2 Reactivity in Homo- and Heterobimetallic Zn and Cu Complexes
abstract: Herein, we investigate the β-thio-δ-diimine (BTDDI) ligand, recently reported as a sulfur containing analogue of the established BODDI framework, as a platform for mono- and bimetallic Cu(I) and Zn(II) chemistry. Sequential metalation enables selective access to homo- and heterobimetallic complexes, including the first structurally characterised Cu/Zn derivative of this ligand class. Replacement of the central oxygen donor by sulfur expands the dinuclear framework, resulting in significantly increased metal–metal separations.

title: Insights into the Degradation Mechanism of Aqueous LiMn2O4-Cathode Interfaces by Computational Vibrational Spectroscopy
abstract: LiMn2O4 (LMO) is a versatile and earth-abundant Li intercalation compound of high interest for sustainable energy storage and conversion. Yet, its broader adoption as a cathode in Li-ion batteries or as a water-splitting electrocatalyst is hindered by severe degradation reactions at the solid-electrolyte interface. This instability is rooted in its mixed-valence Mn3+ / Mn4+ electronic structure, which is governed by the Li content. Still, the atomistic link between the lithiation state and interfacial degradation remains elusive.

title: Operando and Postmortem Study of Iridium-Decorated Titanium-Based Catalysts in PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: Understanding the dynamic degradation of oxygen-evolution electrocatalysts under realistic operating conditions is essential for advancing the performance and efficiency of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers. By combining operando Small-Angle and Wide-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS/WAXS) with electrochemical measurements, the evolution of iridium nanoparticles supported on TiO2, TiC, and TiN, loaded on full membrane electrode assemblies, and undergoing accelerated stress testing in these assemblies has been monitored in real time. SAXS analysis shows pronounced Ostwald ripening of Ir on TiO2, resulting in particle growth from 1.5 to 2.2 nm and a corresponding loss of electrochemically active surface area. In contrast, Ir supported on TiC remains morphologically stable. However, the TiC support undergoes severe degradation, losing approximately 80% crystallinity and releasing Ti species that migrate across the membrane. TiN exhibits an intermediate behavior, showing partial oxidation, moderate Ir growth, and limited Ti migration. Postmortem transmission electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy corroborate results from operando analyses. Results confirm the dissolution and oxidation of Ti in TiC and TiN, as well as the structural stability of TiO2, and better describe the boundaries of the trade-off between nanoparticle stability and support robustness. Moreover, results underscore the need to design catalyst–support systems capable of simultaneously suppressing Ir ripening and mitigating support corrosion. Finally, this study demonstrates the capabilities of operando SAXS/WAXS analysis from full membrane electrode assemblies to elucidate degradation pathways and inform the development of durable, next-generation anode catalysts for PEM electrolyzers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Unlocking Sulfurdiimide Reagents as Radical Traps in the Decarboxylative Synthesis of Sulfinamidines
abstract: Aza-sulfur(IV) and (VI) compounds are emerging motifs in medicinal and crop protection chemistry, creating a demand for new methodologies for their challenging synthesis. Sulfurdiimides, the diaza analogues of sulfur dioxide, remain underexplored in their potential to access aza-sulfur compounds, in particular their use as radical traps has not been reported. Here, we describe the synthesis of a new series of stable unsymmetrical sulfurdiimide reagents, which through choice of N-substituent, can be electronically tuned to unlock radical trapping reactivity. Taking advantage of the wide abundance of commercially available carboxylic acids, we have developed an acridine/copper cocatalyzed decarboxylative addition into sulfurdiimide reagents, to deliver a diverse range of sulfinamidine products. The method is scalable, and exhibits good functional group tolerance, and provides an efficient platform to access complex aza-sulfur(VI) functional groups.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Integrative SMR and multi-model machine learning characterize FCER1A- and INSIG1-associated phenotypes in arterial aging-related disease
abstract: Background and aims : Global population aging has made age-related cardiovascular disease an urgent public health challenge, and inflammation is closely associated with arterial aging. This study aimed to identify inflammation-related molecular features associated with arterial aging-related disease using an integrative analytical framework. Methods : We integrated summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. SMR used FinnGen coronary artery disease GWAS and GTEx v8 whole-blood eQTL data.

title: DMRG for Multi-Component Quantum Systems: A Symmetry-Aware and Unified Framework
abstract: Recent advances in high-resolution spectroscopy and cavity quantum technologies have driven growing interest in multicomponent quantum chemistry, where electronic degrees of freedom are treated on an equal footing with other quantum particles. Here, we present a unified symmetry-aware density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) framework for multicomponent quantum chemistry.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Dominant operating effects and localized material responses in dye removal by MOF based composites: Insights from interpretable machine learning
abstract: Reliable comparison of MOF based composites for dye contaminated water treatment remains challenging because reported removal capacities do not reveal whether performance variations arise from broadly influential operating effects or material responses confined to specific treatment contexts. Here, we developed an interpretable machine learning framework using heterogeneous literature derived experimental records to distinguish broadly influential operating effects from localized material responses.

title: Global dispersal of macroalgae-derived recalcitrant DOC may substantially contribute to deep-ocean carbon storage
abstract: Macroalgae, the dominant primary producers of Earth's most productive coastal vegetated ecosystems and a vital component driving ocean carbon sequestration, produce ∼5 to 80% of their net primary productivity as dissolved organic carbon (DOC). However, the global extent, fate, and contribution of this macroalgae-derived DOC to the pelagic carbon pool remain poorly understood. We establish a molecular fingerprint of the dominant coastal macroalga Saccharina japonica-derived DOC (kelp-derived DOC) using ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and conservative filtering. We differentiate the kelp-derived DOC into labile (LDOC) and recalcitrant fractions (RDOC) based on prolonged resistance to microbial degradation, identify discriminating molecular traits through machine learning, and integrate them into a stability metric, molecular recalcitrance score (MRS). Both candidate kelp-associated RDOC signals and the more persistent, semilabile subset of candidate kelp-associated LDOC signals are detected throughout the global ocean, as far as ∼10,000 kilometers from kelp ecosystems and at depths of ∼5500 meters. Detected candidate kelp-associated DOC signals exhibit elevated MRS, with values positively correlated with distance from source regions, indicating selective long-distance transport of intrinsically more stable compounds. We preliminarily estimate that coastal macroalgal ecosystems globally may contribute 320.7 to 481.1 teragrams of carbon per year of RDOC. The detection of candidate kelp-associated RDOC signals throughout the global ocean provides molecular-level evidence of the long-distance export of macroalgae-derived RDOC to the pelagic and deep ocean, highlighting a major, previously unrecognized pathway of long-term storage of macroalgae-derived DOC in global oceans, although the precise fraction exported to the deep ocean remains to be quantified.

title: Four Ways to Manufacture a Coordination Finding: A Control Battery for Mixed-Motive MARL
abstract: Mixed-motive multi-agent reinforcement-learning sweeps can manufacture findings before analysis. In a four-agent shared-state task, four choices make reward scale look structurally dominant, manufacture a symmetric treatment profile, turn state contention into a general correlation effect, and misattribute attainable-objective costs to learning. The treatment is signed correlation among target coordinates (ideal points), not a manipulation of objective- or reward-function alignment.

title: Chemical Profiling and Authentication of Boswellia Species and Frankincense Products: Advances in Metabolomics and Quality Markers
abstract: Frankincense is an aromatic oleo-gum resin obtained from Boswellia species and is widely used in traditional medicine, pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, perfumery, and incense products. Its expanding trade has intensified concerns over species substitution, geographical mislabeling, adulteration, compositional variability, and inconsistent product quality.

title: Fragment-Based Representation Learning for Polymers and Heterogeneous Formulations
Multi-omics integration identifies Acsm2/ACSM2A deficiency as a metabolic driver of ZBP1-mediated PANoptosis in acute kidney injury
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) converges on tubular epithelial cell (TEC) death and metabolic collapse, fueling the transition to chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the molecular link between metabolic failure and inflammatory cell death remains poorly defined. Here, we integrated cross-model transcriptomics of three mechanistically distinct murine AKI models with single-cell RNA-seq, high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning feature selection. This multi-omics framework identified acyl-CoA synthetase medium-chain family member 2 (Acsm2), a rate-limiting mitochondrial enzyme for medium-chain fatty acid β-oxidation, as the top conserved hub gene suppressed in injured proximal tubule cells. Acsm2/ACSM2A downregulation was confirmed in mouse AKI models and in human HK-2 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R). ACSM2A deficiency alone was sufficient to simultaneously activate apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis, indicative of PANoptosis, whereas restoration of ACSM2A expression attenuated OGD/R-induced cell death. Mechanistically, ACSM2A loss provoked mitochondrial oxidative stress and drove the accumulation of Z-form nucleic acids. Scavenging mitochondrial reactive oxygen species or silencing ZBP1 rescued cells from ACSM2A knockdown-induced cell death, implicating ZBP1 as a downstream mediator. Collectively, our findings establish ACSM2A loss as a trigger of ZBP1-dependent PANoptosis in TECs and position the ACSM2A-ZBP1 axis as a candidate pathogenic mechanism that warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic node for intercepting the AKI-to-CKD transition.
venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

title: Application of a semi-supervised learning framework combining principal component constraint enhancement in near-infrared spectroscopy of Rhizome Coptidis
abstract: Rhizome Coptidis is a popular traditional Chinese medicinal herb, and analyzing its composition is crucial for evaluating its quality. However, existing analytical methods can produce significantly different results due to various practical factors, so there is an urgent need to develop more suitable analytical methods. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR) is widely used in the analysis of traditional Chinese medicine due to its rapid, non-destructive, and pollution-free characteristics. It offers numerous possibilities for the detection of Rhizome Coptidis.
venue: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy

title: Evaluation of U-Net based architectures for synthetic CT generation from dual-contrast MRI
abstract: Deep learning-based MRI-to-CT synthesis supports MR-only radiotherapy and PET/MR attenuation correction, but comparisons of U-Net variants are confounded by differences in datasets, preprocessing, training protocols, and evaluation metrics. This study performed a controlled, tissue-aware, and complexity-aware comparison of five U-Net-based architectures, including U-Net, ResU-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and attention deep residual U-Net (ADR-U-Net), for brain sCT generation from T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI in 37 subjects from the CERMEP-IDB-MRXFDG database.

title: Beyond Direct Two-Electron Oxidation: High-Potential Formaldehyde Oxidation on Palladium Still Generates Hydrogen Atoms
abstract: Electrochemical oxidation is typically regarded as incompatible with hydrogen intermediate formation, particularly at highly positive potentials where surface hydrogen species are expected to be rapidly oxidized. Formaldehyde oxidation reaction (FOR) on palladium represents a prominent example: low-potential FOR has been associated with hydrogen generation, whereas high-potential FOR is commonly interpreted as a direct two-electron oxidation to formate that bypasses hydrogen intermediates. Here we challenge this conventional view using a Janus palladium membrane electrode (J-Pdm) that spatially decouples hydrogen generation, absorption, permeation, and detection. By monitoring the hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) current on the electrochemically isolated detection side of J-Pdm, we directly quantify hydrogen atoms generated during FOR under alkaline conditions. Unexpectedly, permeated hydrogen remains detectable over a broad FOR potential window up to 1.5 V vs RHE (reversible hydrogen electrode), demonstrating that high-potential FOR on Pd is not a hydrogen-free oxidation process. Coulometric measurements confirm hydrogen uptake within the Pd lattice, with H/Pd ratios reaching up to 0.57. Spectroscopic and computational results support a sequential hydrogen-generating oxidation mechanism in which formaldehyde-derived intermediates undergo favorable C–H activation, while the resulting hydrogen atoms compete among absorption into the Pd lattice, recombination to H2, and oxidation to protons. FOR-generated hydrogen atoms can be utilized for styrene hydrogenation in an organic phase, establishing anodic hydrogenation as a viable electrosynthetic strategy. These findings provide new mechanistic understanding of formaldehyde oxidation on palladium and also demonstrate J-Pdm as a powerful platform for detecting and utilizing transient hydrogen intermediates in anodic reactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Small Sample Machine Learning for Predicting Composition Changes in Chemically Pretreated Kapok Fiber
abstract: Kapok is a lightweight hollow tropical fiber with potential as a renewable feedstock, but its waxy surface and lignin-containing matrix complicate aqueous processing. This study evaluated whether limited-data machine learning could predict kapok fiber composition after aqueous chemical pretreatment using only three process descriptors. Kapok fibers were pretreated using dilute H2SO4, hydrothermal water, and NaOH across a shared window of residence time, temperature and pH-associated pretreatment environment. A data set of 33 pretreatment runs was constructed, with cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin contents used as composition targets after correction with solid yield. Single-output and wrapper-based multitarget regression models were screened and then evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation to reduce dependence on a single train-test split. The LOOCV results showed target-dependent predictability. In single-output modeling, cellulose was the most predictable component, with GBDT giving the strongest performance (R 2 = 0.782; RMSE = 4.185 percentage points), whereas hemicellulose and lignin showed weaker prediction. In wrapper-based multitarget modeling, GBDT improved simultaneous prediction of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, giving R 2 values of 0.909, 0.653, and 0.672, respectively. Feature-importance analysis indicated that temperature was the dominant descriptor for polysaccharide-related composition changes, whereas the pH-associated pretreatment environment contributed more strongly to lignin-related variation. These findings position limited-data machine learning as a useful exploratory tool for modeling pretreatment-composition relationships in kapok fiber, while also highlighting the need for cautious validation when sample size is small.

title: Postnatal Development Shapes the Cardiac Response to Milrinone
abstract: Background: Milrinone, a phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE-3) inhibitor, is widely used to improve cardiac output in pediatric and adult patients. Yet, developmental differences in myocardial responsiveness to milrinone remain incompletely understood. In this study, we examined the impact of postnatal maturation on the acute cardiac effects of milrinone using an intact guinea pig heart model. Methods: Neonatal (0-2 days), juvenile (4-10 days), and adult (> 6 months) guinea pig hearts were excised, Langendorff-perfused, and cardiac metrics were evaluated under basal conditions and in response to acute milrinone treatment (15 minutes, 10 and 100 M sequential concentrations). Pseudo-electrocardiograms were recorded continuously and left ventricular pressure measurements were performed under sinus rhythm and in response to external pacing. Post-rest potentiation was used to assess contractile reserve, and optical action potentials and calcium transients were recorded. Results: Baseline left ventricular developed pressure (LVDP), action potential duration (APD), and calcium transient duration (CaD) increased with postnatal maturation, consistent with developmental cardiomyocyte remodeling and refinement of excitation-contraction coupling. Milrinone increased heart rate in all age groups, with the greatest chronotropic response at 100 M. Milrinone also increased ventricular contractility and relaxation across developmental stages, but the magnitude of the response varied with age and was attenuated during high frequency pacing. Adult hearts had the greatest increase in LVDP during sinus rhythm and robust post-rest potentiation, which were less pronounced in neonatal hearts. APD and CaD were shortened in neonatal and adult hearts, but were minimally affected in juveniles, indicating a non-linear developmental pattern. Conclusions: Milrinone exerts positive chronotropic, inotropic, and lusitropic effects throughout development, but the magnitude and frequency dependence of these responses vary with age. These findings suggest that postnatal maturation influences the cardiac response to PDE3 inhibition. These developmental differences highlight the importance of considering age as a biological factor in pediatric drug selection and dosing.

title: SCOPE: From Shape and Color to Binding Affinity, with Confidence
abstract: Three-dimensional quantitative structure–activity relationship (3D-QSAR) is widely used in lead optimization in drug discovery, yet prediction reliability remains underexplored despite the continued expansion of chemical space. Here, we present SCOPE ( S hape and Co lor-based P rediction E nsemble), a confidence-aware ensemble model for binding affinity prediction that incorporates a target-agnostic applicability domain mapping molecular similarity to prediction confidence.

title: Zero-shot emotional speech synthesis based on feature decoupling and adaptive loss-threshold reweighting
abstract: Deep learning-based zero-shot speech synthesis has achieved substantial progress in speaker generalization, but stable modeling remains challenging in fine-grained emotional scenarios. Existing systems often process textual and emotional conditions through shared or closely coupled pathways, which may introduce interference between semantic content and emotional expression. In addition, uniformly averaging per-sample Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) losses may provide insufficient optimization emphasis to high-loss emotional samples. This study proposes a CFM-based zero-shot emotional speech synthesis method. Emotion-Text Decoupling Attention (ETDA) processes semantic and emotional conditions through parallel cross-attention streams and combines them through adaptive gated fusion, allowing the two conditions to retain their respective information before fusion. A 16-class fine-grained emotion space is constructed through classifier filtering and K-Means clustering based on pitch and energy features, and the resulting labels are mapped to continuous representations using a trainable lookup embedding. During training, Adaptive Loss-Threshold Reweighting estimates a threshold from mini-batch loss statistics and assigns larger weights to samples whose individual CFM losses exceed that threshold. Under speaker-disjoint evaluation on ESD, the proposed method achieves a word error rate of 3.62±0.06%, a mel-cepstral distortion of 4.45±0.05 dB, and an emotional expressiveness mean opinion score of 4.64±0.04. Controlled text-length expansion and analyses on a fixed subset of high-loss emotional samples further indicate that the proposed method maintains linguistic content and emotional expression more consistently under the evaluated conditions. These results suggest that the proposed method can, to some extent, improve content preservation, emotional expression, and acoustic reconstruction in fine-grained zero-shot emotional speech synthesis.

title: Evaluation of pre-trained models for pedagogical assessment of novel AI-assisted educational questions
abstract: The surge in AI-assisted generation of educational materials has outpaced our capacity to validate their pedagogical quality. Automated evaluation using Bloom Classifier models is a promising approach to assess educational materials at scale. These models show high accuracy within-distribution dataset (IID Dataset). However, applying the same models to new out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets such as AI-assisted generated questions could show performance degradation. To identify robust classifiers under dataset shift, we evaluated traditional Machine Learning (ML), transformer, and Large Language models on the Bloom level classification task. We also explored feature-engineering strategies incorporating NLP metrics, appending the learning objectives as part of the input, and text splicing to stabilize OOD performance. Our baseline tests show that TFPOS-IDF ML models perform poorly on OOD (Macro F1-score 0.48) compared to BERT (0.55) and LLMs (0.79). Text splicing improved macro F1-score performance of ML and BERT models (0.59 and 0.62, respectively). Appending the learning objectives with the input increased model performance on specific dataset. Model retraining provided the largest improvement across models and datasets. Overall, these findings highlight the trade-off on the use of pre-trained models with novel AI-assisted educational questions and how strategic feature enhancements help address loss in performance.

title: Uncertainty prediction in composite quantum chemistry approaches
abstract: In this work, we consider the problem of uncertainty estimation of the results obtained through theoretical calculations using a composite quantum chemistry scheme. Each component of the composite scheme carries its own individual uncertainty, originating principally from a finite size of the basis set used in the calculations. Of practical interest is the total uncertainty, i.e. the uncertainty of the sum of all components. We first show that the conventional error propagation rules that treat each component as a statistically uncorrelated variable are not well-justified in practice. To remedy this, we propose a method of estimating the total uncertainty of the composite scheme which does not rely on the assumption that the components are independent. It is formulated as a series of random walks with different starting values that represent the uncertainty of each component of the composite scheme. This method is first applied to two example composite schemes for the water dimer and the nitrogen molecule that illustrate its most salient features and allow for a deeper analysis. Next, the method is tested for a larger set of interaction energies from the S66 dataset for which trustworthy reference data are available and the error can be assessed unambiguously. It is shown that the method provides reliable and reasonably tight uncertainty estimates at an arbitrary predefined confidence level required in a given application. While the focus of the paper is on composite schemes, we believe that the general idea can be useful more broadly in computational chemistry and physics.

title: SMILESGNN: Interpretable Clinical Toxicity Prediction via SMILES-Graph Cross-Attention Fusion
